info.description:
# Introduction

Welcome to the Agicap Supplier API documentation. This API is designed to help you synchronise your supplier referential from a third-party source of truth into Agicap.

### Suppliers overview

A **supplier** represents the business entity that issues invoices to your company — a service provider, contractor, or any third party you purchase from. It carries the supplier's identity (legal name, legal ID, address, contacts) and serves as the reference object for supplier invoice management and pre-accounting workflows.

Suppliers are **distinct from beneficiaries**. A beneficiary represents a bank account to which a payment is sent. The same supplier may have several beneficiaries (multiple bank accounts), and a single beneficiary may be shared across suppliers (e.g. a factoring company collecting on behalf of multiple suppliers). To synchronise beneficiaries and link them to their suppliers, refer to the Agicap Payment API documentation.

### Use case covered by this API

#### Synchronise your supplier referential from your ERP

Agicap provides a supplier referential that enables finance teams to centralise supplier master data, and use it for their P2P workflow. If your source of truth lives in a third-party system (ERP, procurement tool, accounting software), this API lets you push your supplier data into Agicap and keep it in sync.

The synchronisation endpoint lets you bulk-upsert your full supplier list in a single call. The sync key is the **supplier identifier in your ERP** (`erpId`): if a supplier already exists for a given `erpId`, it is updated rather than duplicated; otherwise a new supplier is created. Suppliers absent from the synchronisation payload are automatically deleted from Agicap.

**Linking suppliers to beneficiaries** — in Agicap, a supplier and its beneficiaries are two distinct objects. Linking them is what enables the full P2P workflow: supplier invoice management, payment preparation and execution, and pre-accounting rely on knowing which bank account belongs to which supplier. The link is established at beneficiary sync time via the `supplierErpId` field. The recommended call order is therefore:

1. Sync suppliers first using this API.
2. Sync beneficiaries and establish the links using the Agicap Payment API — refer to its documentation for details.

### Prerequisites for using this API

**Activate the right module.** You need to activate the Accounts Payable module on your entity. Contact your Account Manager to activate the appropriate solution depending on your needs.

### Authentication

To call this API, you need API credentials with a specific scope. Each route in the Agicap Supplier API documentation will specify the required scope.

Steps to obtain the right scope for your credentials:

1. **Generate API Credentials.** Follow the [Authentication guidelines](https://api.agicap.com/guides/authentication) to generate your API credentials.
2. **Select the Required Scope.** Ensure you select the necessary scope when generating these credentials.
3. **Generate your Access Token.** Use the Authentication API to generate your access token. Be sure to specify the required scope in your request.
4. **Use the Authentication Token.** Include this authentication token in your requests to the Supplier API.

This documentation aims to guide you through the process of integrating and using the Agicap Supplier API effectively. If you have any questions or need further assistance, feel free to reach out to our support team.

get.description:
Returns the suppliers of an entity using cursor-based pagination, so ERP Connectivity can
diff its catalog against Agicap. Pass the nextCursor of a previous page to fetch the next one.
Use the optional erpId filter to look up a single supplier.

parameters.description: Optional filter on a single ERP identifier.
parameters.name: erpId

parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned as nextCursor by the previous page.
parameters.name: cursor

parameters.description: Maximum number of suppliers per page (1 to 1000, default 1000).
parameters.name: limit

200.description: Your request has been successfully processed.

429.description: Too many requests. Please try again later.

get.summary: List the suppliers of an entity

post.description:
Pushes up to 1000 suppliers (create / update / delete) for an entity in a single call.
Processing is synchronous and returns a syncId usable to fetch the row-by-row errors.
If the same erpId appears more than once in a batch, all of its occurrences are rejected and reported as row errors.

200.description: Your request has been successfully processed.

429.description: Too many requests. Please try again later.

get.description:
Returns the row-by-row errors of a previous synchronization, paginated.
The syncId is the one returned by the synchronize endpoint.

parameters.description: Synchronization identifier returned by the synchronize endpoint.
parameters.name: syncId

parameters.description: Opaque cursor returned as cursor.after by the previous page. Omit to fetch the first page.
parameters.name: after

200.description: Your request has been successfully processed.

429.description: Too many requests. Please try again later.
